script.title: Cash is not safe: what 3% inflation does to $10,000

scenes.heading: Is cash safe?
scenes.narration: Money in a drawer never goes down. Or does it? Here is what inflation does to cash.
scenes.visual_brief:
#pergunta Is cash really safe?
Open the loop.

scenes.heading: Prices go up
scenes.narration: Inflation means prices rise over time, so the same $100 buys less every year. The US government tracks this with the Consumer Price Index.

scenes.heading: The example
scenes.narration: Our example assumes 3% inflation a year. Prices compound, just like interest. And cash in a drawer earns nothing.
scenes.visual_brief:
#lista 3% inflation a year, assumed; Prices compound like interest; Cash earns nothing
Assumptions.

scenes.heading: Half in 24 years
scenes.narration: Use the Rule of 72 backwards: 72 divided by 3 is 24. At 3% inflation, cash loses half its buying power in about 24 years.
scenes.visual_brief:
#numero 24 | years for cash to lose half its buying power at 3%
Rule of 72.

scenes.heading: What $100 buys
scenes.narration: Today your $100 buys $100 of stuff. In 10 years, about $74 worth. In 20 years, about $55.
scenes.visual_brief:
#grafico What $100 in cash buys, at 3% inflation | Today=100; In 10 years=74; In 20 years=55
The slide.

scenes.heading: $10,000 in a drawer
scenes.narration: Put $10,000 in cash today, and in 10 years it buys only what $7,441 buys now.
scenes.visual_brief:
#numero 7441 | dollars of buying power left from $10,000 after 10 years
The silent loss.

scenes.heading: Why it happens
scenes.narration: Prices go up, your cash stays the same, so every year it buys a little less. Nothing is taken from your account. It just shrinks in what it can do.
scenes.visual_brief:
#causa Prices rise 3% a year => Your cash stays the same => You can buy less
The mechanism.

scenes.heading: Keeping up
scenes.narration: To keep up, your money has to grow at least as fast as prices. Below the inflation rate, you are losing buying power, even if the number on the screen goes up.
scenes.visual_brief:
#comparacao Cash: grows 0%; loses to inflation | Money that keeps up: grows at least 3% a year; holds its buying power
The bar to clear.

scenes.heading: Check the real numbers
scenes.narration: You can check real US inflation for any period with the free CPI Inflation Calculator from the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The link is in the description.

scenes.heading: Cash has a job
scenes.narration: Cash is great for emergencies and short term goals. For long term goals, remember the silent 3%. This is math, not financial advice.

claims.text: At 3% a year, $100 buys about $74 of today's goods in 10 years (100/1.03^10 = 74.4) and about $55 in 20 years (55.4). Calculo proprio.
At 3% inflation, $10,000 in cash buys what $7,441 buys today after 10 years. Calculo proprio.
By the Rule of 72, 72 divided by 3 is 24: at 3% a year, prices double, and cash loses half its buying power, in about 24 years.
The BLS CPI Inflation Calculator compares the buying power of a dollar between two dates.
